svg.title: Ahmed Al Rafsan, aeronautical engineer and AI engineer. A technical drawing of my conceptual aircraft, my thesis composite laminate and a neural network that predicts deflection and stress.

text.tspan: Trained in aircraft design and finite-element analysis.
Now I build AI and machine-learning systems, and
I keep returning to where my two fields meet:
models that make engineering analysis faster
without making it any less trustworthy.

svg.title: Technical drawing: top view of my conceptual aircraft with an 8.0 metre span and 12.0 metre length and a finite-element mesh on one wing; detail B shows my thesis three-ply composite laminate; a section through the wing; and a small neural network that predicts deflection and stress from fibre angle, thickness and load.

g.text: Each ply 0.125 mm. θ swept −45° to +45°: 19 lay-ups.
Inputs θ, t, p. Outputs δ, σ. No full simulation.

text.tspan: Drawn from my own work: the top view of my conceptual aircraft (span, length,
wing area, taper), Detail B is my thesis laminate, and the blue network is the
machine-learning layer that ties the two fields together.
